theorem_title: Exact realization of blind coalitions by Boolean generators
natural_language_statement:
Let $I,J$ be arbitrary types and $F:J\times I\to\{0,1\}$ a Boolean family. Construct a base state $*$ with target 0 and a state $[j]$ of target 1 for each $j\in J$. Observer $i$ returns 0 at the base and $1-F(j,i)$ at $[j]$. A coalition $S\subseteq I$ is blind when two states have different targets but equal observations on every $i\in S$. Then

$$
S\text{ is blind}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\exists j\in J\ \forall i\in S,\ F(j,i)=1.
$$

This realizes exactly the family of coalitions lying below at least one Boolean generator. No finiteness or nonemptiness assumptions on either index type are required.
formal_statement:
theorem NewMathDiscovery.BlindnessRealization.blind_iff_below_generator {I J : Type} (F : J → I → Bool)
    (S : I → Prop) :
    Blind S (State.observe F) State.target ↔
      ∃ j, ∀ i, S i → F j i = true := by sorry
